jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager , AWS Organizations
jobs.description:
Description

We are looking for an experienced Technical Program Manager to tackle complex and ambiguous problems that span numerous systems and organizations across AMG's portfolio. You will be a highly visible leader who owns the communication, coordination, and execution of multi-year program vision across AWS Organizations, Accounts, and Control Tower.

You will work with senior product and engineering leaders to define strategy and requirements. You will design, coordinate, and execute technical solutions that scale globally across AWS's multi-account and governance ecosystem. Managing numerous complex systems and cross-service integrations, you will make appropriate trade-offs between business and technical constraints, clearly communicate goals, roles, and responsibilities. Working cross-functionally, you will identify and secure commitment from tech teams across AWS for new initiatives, driving consensus on the technical approach.

The ideal candidate will have a well-rounded technical background and a history of leading large programs end-to-end. They will own efforts to coordinate and unify roadmaps and technical direction across multiple complex governance and account management systems. They will identify opportunities to converge overlapping technical efforts and drive long-term strategy across AMG's three pillars. Maturity, high-level judgment, negotiation skills, ability to influence, analytical talent, and leadership are essential to success.

If you're looking for a chance to shape how every AWS customer — from startups to the largest enterprises — secures and governs their cloud environment; if you want to work at the intersection of security, policy management, and large-scale distributed systems; if you're excited about AI-native operations and how agents can transform the developer experience for cloud governance — then this is the role for you. Come work with our team of engineers, product managers, and technical leaders building the foundational layer of AWS.

About The Team

AWS Accounts Management & Governance (AMG) provides the foundation for how customers set up, secure, and scale their AWS environments. AWS Accounts offers a fast, simple entry point to the cloud. AWS Organizations delivers consistent governance and security across accounts at any scale. AWS Control Tower enforces best practices through an automated, opinionated landing zone from day one.

Together, these services help customers securely govern and manage their multi-account environments — growing with confidence that their infrastructure is secure by default and fully aligned with their security and compliance requirements. For internal AWS services, AMG provides the core primitives that enable multi-account and multi-organization service delivery across the AWS ecosystem. We continue to invest across three pillars: security and compliance, scaling, and ease of use.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
5+ years of technical program management experience
Strong verbal/written communication and presentation skills — ability to clearly communicate high-level strategy as well as technical details
Expertise with AI/ML-assisted development workflows and agentic automation.
Experience driving technical strategy and architecture decisions, especially for large-scale distributed systems
Experience collaborating with product, engineering, and non-technical partners
Prior experience working on large cross-org programs with extensive technical deep-dive skills
Track record for delivering quality products on time

Preferred Qualifications

Master's Degree in Computer Science or equivalent industry experience
Experience working with a diverse team of engineers, product managers, scientists, and senior leaders
Experience in non-technical aspects including business analysis (e.g., SQL) and process optimization
Experience with agile/iterative development and program management methodologies
Demonstrated passion for understanding ambiguous, complex problems and driving high-quality, innovative, and robust technical solutions
Knowledge of software engineering best practices including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations

jobs.title: Principal Program Manager, Whole Foods Market Central Kitchen Strategy, Whole Foods Market Culinary Merchandising
jobs.description:
Description

Whole Foods Market is seeking a Principal Program Manager to help shape the future of how we produce freshly prepared food in centralized commissary kitchens. This is a strategic, senior role for someone who thrives in ambiguity and can define strategy where little exists today. Working across Amazon VP organizations and with senior leadership at WFM and Amazon, you will lead a significant, complex initiative from concept through execution, building the business case, aligning stakeholders, and standing up the mechanisms needed to deliver. The ideal candidate pairs deep strategic program management experience with a strong understanding of food service, kitchen production, supply chain, food safety, and multi-unit retail operations, and can influence and align senior leaders across culinary merchandising, supply chain, operations, finance, and technology.

Key job responsibilities

Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for a significant, complex initiative, driving clarity where the business problem and strategy are not yet fully defined.
Build out business cases and financial plans, framing capital, operational, and strategic tradeoffs for senior leaders and grounding recommendations in data.
Partner across merchandising, supply chain, operations, quality assurance and food safety, finance, technology, and other functional teams to align the organization on a coherent operating model and clear ownership.
Establish the planning, forecasting, and performance mechanisms needed to run the program and measure its success.
Design and launch pilots to validate our strategy, including clear learning plans, and create the stage gates that govern how and when the program scales.
Prepare and drive executive-ready reviews, business cases, and PR/FAQ and narrative documents, representing complex decisions and tradeoffs clearly to VPs and, when needed, SVPs.
Identify and mitigate program risks, building in the redundancy and contingency needed to protect continuity of service to stores and customers.
Actively develop the program management community through mentoring, promotion assessments, and best-practice sharing.
Travel Requirements: Approximately 30% travel to facilities, stores, and partner sites may be required.

About The Team

Our team is at the heart of transforming how customers experience fresh, prepared food at Whole Foods Market and Worldwide Grocery Stores. We set the category strategy and define production models that shape what lands on shelves and in shopping baskets across hundreds of stores nationwide. We work at the intersection of food, data, operations, and retail, partnering closely with supply chain, private brands, operations, e-commerce, finance, and technology to bring innovative, high-quality food programs to life. Our culture rewards curiosity, deep ownership, and creative problem-solving. If you are energized by building something new that directly shapes what customers eat every day, this is the team for you.

Basic Qualifications

7+ years of program or project management experience
7+ years of managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership experience
Bachelor's degree
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
Experience owning program strategy and end to end delivery
Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements
Experience in food production
Deep knowledge of food production and kitchen operations, supply chain and distribution, and the associated food safety and regulatory controls.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience delivering projects within scope, time, budget and quality
MBA
Experience working in a physical store
Experience designing or scaling fresh food production and distribution networks.
Working knowledge of food safety systems (HACCP), allergen and labeling requirements, and quality assurance at scale.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Trade Planning, Worldwide Grocery Category Management (WWGCM)
jobs.description:
Description

Interested in working on an innovative and high-impact business that is changing the way customers think about buying groceries? Our team focuses on creating exceptional shopping experiences that transform how customers discover and purchase perishable goods from Amazon. We're passionate about building compelling assortment, optimizing the customer journey, and developing strategic partnerships to drive category growth. We work in a collaborative environment where innovative thinking and strategic execution are highly valued. Our team strives to deliver exceptional value to customers while driving business results through data-driven decision making.

The Trade Planning PM is responsible for defining the desired shopping experience across Protein, Center-Store Frozen, and Emerging Brands for our multi-banner events and promotional strategies, ensuring a cohesive customer journey. The PM establishes performance standards by defining the requirements for seasonal events, effectively balancing customer satisfaction with financial targets.

In this role, you will own planning programs and analytical mechanisms that inform seasonal event strategy, assortment decisions, and customer experience planning across Worldwide Grocery Stores. You will partner closely with Category, Marketing, Demand Planning, and Supply Chain teams to develop scalable planning frameworks that improve how we select, merchandise, and present products to customers across our grocery formats.

The successful candidate will demonstrate strong business judgment, analytical rigor, and the ability to operate effectively in ambiguous environments. You should be comfortable influencing stakeholders across multiple organizations, defining requirements for new programs and tools, and driving initiatives from concept through implementation. High judgment, analytical talent, and exceptional communication skills are essential for success in this role.

Key job responsibilities

Our environment is fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous. This requires someone who is flexible, detail-oriented, analytical, and comfortable working with multiple teams and other stakeholders.

On a Day To Day Basis, You Will

Own planning programs and mechanisms that support seasonal events and promotional strategies across Worldwide Grocery Stores.
Partner with Category, Marketing, Demand Planning, and Supply Chain teams to develop scalable planning frameworks that improve customer experience and business performance.
Build data-driven selection guidance and category prioritization frameworks that help Protein, Center Store Frozen, and Emerging Brands teams determine the right products, categories, and customer experiences to feature across key seasonal events.
Drive end-to-end program management, including problem discovery, requirements definition, stakeholder alignment, launch readiness, execution, and post-event analysis.
Serve as a key liaison between Category and partner organizations, ensuring stakeholders are aligned on priorities, timelines, and business objectives.
Develop business reviews, leadership updates, and strategic recommendations that influence planning decisions across the Protein, Center Store Frozen, and Emerging Brands organization.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of program or project management experience
3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
3+ years of driving process improvements experience
Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

jobs.title: Perinatal and Pediatric Services Program Manager
jobs.description:
POSITION TITLE:
Perinatal and Pediatric Services Program Manager

REPORTS TO (TITLE):
Chief Operating Officer (COO)

SALARY RANGE:
$90,000 - $123,521 DOE

Job Summary:
The Perinatal and Pediatric Services Program Manager provides operational leadership and oversight of Santa Rosa Community Health’s mobile and community-based health services with the goal of expanding access to perinatal, pediatric, developmental, behavioral health, and family support services for pregnant and postpartum individuals, children birth through age five, and families facing barriers to care. The Perinatal and Pediatric Services Program Manager will also oversee the Comprehensive Perinatal Services Program (CPSP) with services provided at campuses and via mobile health van and at community hubs.

This role will oversee all operational and budgetary components of mobile clinic and community-based operations including, but not limited to staffing, access, coordination and coordination with community partners budgets, reporting, performance improvement, and regulatory readiness in collaboration with clinical, operational, quality, finance, technology, community engagement, and executive leaders.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic, Operational, and Workforce Leadership

Leads mobile and community-based health expansion efforts including the planning and implementation of mobile health services, ensuring strong workflows are created and monitored and that services offered meet community needs.
Translates goals into workflows, staffing models, timelines, performance measures, and accountable deliverables.
Supervises, develops, and supports assigned staff through coaching, training, scheduling, workforce planning, and performance management.
Advises the COO on performance, risks, access barriers, resource needs, and improvement priorities.
Builds a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable team culture.

Mobile Clinic Operations and Patient Access

Oversees daily mobile clinic operations, including schedules, staffing, patient flow, supplies, equipment, technology, safety, and partner-site logistics.
Maintains workflows for outreach, registration, scheduling, documentation, referrals, follow-up, and transitions between mobile and clinic-based care.
Ensures timely access, continuity, coordination, and positive patient experience for families facing barriers to care.

Community Partnerships and Engagement

Fosters strong partnerships with organizations serving pregnant and postpartum individuals, children, caregivers, and families. Works collaboratively with partners to understand community needs and respond effectively.
Coordinates outreach, referral pathways, partner meetings, and culturally responsive materials with community and internal teams.
Evaluates mobile and community-based clinic locations based on need, accessibility, safety, privacy, geographic coverage, and operational feasibility.
Represents Santa Rosa Community Health in funder meetings, collaborative planning, implementation reviews, and community learning activities.

Financial and Resource Management

Develops and monitors the program budget, staffing allocations, productivity targets, supply/equipment expenses, and grant-funded expenditures.
Reviews financial and operational performance, addresses variances with the COO, and supports sustainability planning.
Ensures appropriate use of resources in accordance with organizational policies, funding requirements, and payroll/timekeeping processes.

Quality, Compliance, and Risk Management

Leads quality improvement and monitors access, service, patient experience, safety, and outcome measures.
Oversees complaints, grievances, safety concerns, corrective action plans, audits, funder reviews, and regulatory assessments.
Ensures compliance with policies, protocols, privacy requirements, data-sharing agreements, and applicable regulations.
Maintains patient confidentiality and promptly reports unusual incidents or practices inconsistent with organizational policy.

CPSP Oversight

Oversees CPSP Coordinator performance across SRCH campuses to support safe, consistent care for participating patients.
Oversees CPSP requirements across participating sites, ensuring site information remains current with Partnership HealthPlan of California (PHP) and the California Department of Public Health (CDPH).
Coordinates updates to CPSP provider lists, including adding perinatal coordinators and clinicians as appropriate.
Ensures CPSP protocols remain current and are consistently followed by perinatal coordinators.

Data, Evaluation, and Reporting

Develops dashboards and reports on clinic events, services, referrals, continuity, demographics, patient experience, and program objectives.
Ensures program data are accurate, complete, timely, documented, and used to improve quality, access, equity, and service delivery.
Coordinates required screening data, demographic information, quarterly reports, program narratives, funder evaluation, training, and shared-learning activities.

Systems, Training, and Change Management

Leads implementation and optimization of systems, technology, EHR workflows, reporting, and operational processes supporting mobile health services.
Develops competencies, onboarding materials, training plans, procedures, job aids, and staff training for mobile workflows and program requirements.
Plans and facilitates effective meetings that promote engagement, accountability, and follow-through.

Collaboration and Organizational Leadership

Partners with clinical, nursing, behavioral health, patient access, quality, finance, HR, IT, facilities, and administrative leaders to clarify roles, decisions, responsibilities, and deadlines.
Shares best practices and contributes to organization-wide standardization, improvement, and concise leadership updates.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in health care administration, public health, nursing, social work, business administration, or a related field; at least four years of progressively responsible related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience required.
Minimum four years of health care operations or program-management experience preferred.
Minimum four years of supervisory experience, including oversight of supervisors, managers, or multidisciplinary teams, preferred.
Complex, multisite, community-based, or mobile clinical operations experience strongly preferred.
Experience in a Federally Qualified Health Center, safety-net health system, maternal and child health program, or publicly funded health initiative preferred.
Bilingual English and Spanish, or another language reflective of the patient population, preferred.

Knowledge And Skills

Strong strategic, operational, financial, and program-management skills.
Advanced knowledge of clinical operations, patient access, scheduling, patient flow, staffing, and front- and back-office workflows.
Demonstrated ability to improve systems, standardize workflows, and lead change.
Experience with quality improvement, compliance, data reporting, and regulatory readiness.
Strong leadership, coaching, team-building, communication, facilitation, and conflict-resolution skills.
Ability to analyze complex information, solve problems, exercise good judgment, and manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Demonstrated commitment to health equity, cultural responsiveness, language access, and family-centered care.
Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Experience with Epic or another electronic health record preferred.
Knowledge of developmental screening tools, including but not limited to ASQ, preferred.
Current CPR certification.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation required.

SRCH is an equal opportunity employer to all, regardless of age, ancestry, color, disability (mental and physical), exercising the right to family care and medical leave, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, military or veteran status, national origin, political affiliation, race, religious creed, sex (includes pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), and sexual orientation.

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, this position is frequently required to do the following:

Use standard office equipment and access, input, and retrieve information from a computer. Use computer keyboard with manual and finger dexterity and wrist-finger speed sufficient to perform repetitive actions efficiently for extended periods of time.
Communicate effectively in person, virtually, and by telephone in a manner which can be understood by those with whom the person is speaking, including a diverse population.
Give and follow verbal and written instructions with attention to detail and accuracy.
Perform complex mental functions and basic arithmetic functions; interpret complex laws, regulations, and policies; collect, interpret, and/or analyze complex data and information.
Vision: see details of objects at close range.
Coordinate multiple tasks simultaneously.
Enter, exit, and work within a mobile clinic environment.
Reach forward, up, down, and to the side.
Sit or stand for minimum periods of one hour at a time and come and go from the work area repeatedly throughout the day.
Tolerate working outside in fluctuating weather conditions, including hot and cold temperatures and occasional wet weather.
Reliable transportation.
May drive SRCH mobile van/s, as needed.
Coordinate multiple tasks simultaneously.
Ability to travel between Santa Rosa Community Health locations and community partner sites.
Lift up to ten (10) pounds.

SRCH provides reasonable accommodation for individuals with a physical or mental disability to apply for jobs and to perform the essential functions of their jobs unless it would cause an undue hardship.

jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Advanced Development
jobs.description:
Joby Advanced Development designs, develops, and flight-tests novel aircraft using a software-first autonomy approach. We build and deploy autonomy, perception, planning, and radar systems across conventional, electric, and hydrogen-electric aircraft in both CTOL and VTOL configurations.

Overview

As a Staff Program Manager in the Advanced Development group, you will serve as a strategic program lead across multi-disciplinary engineering teams, directly driving execution and alignment for the J208 program. You will take primary responsibility for overall program execution, financial oversight, and integrated master schedule performance across multiple domains. In this role, you will evaluate broad system interdependencies, solve for complex critical path issues and bottlenecks before they impact strategic objectives, and serve as a decision-maker and thought leader across technical workstreams.

Responsibilities

Direct, evaluate, and report on total J208 program schedule performance and financial health, developing complex forecasting models across engineering workstreams
Partner with engineering leads and cross-functional teams to map complex multi-tier project dependencies, identify critical path drivers, and proactively resolve systemic program bottlenecks
Integrate with Finance to track, analyze, and optimize total program cost performance, aligning budget forecasts with overarching company objectives
Understand and solve for advanced or unique schedule, resource, or technical constraints, developing or selecting new program management tools, methods, and frameworks to maintain program momentum
Facilitate strategic cross-functional alignment and build coalitions across technical hardware, software, flight test, and business operations teams to manage down-the-line system impacts and interdependencies
Develop program management standards, concepts, and reporting frameworks, while mentoring and directing team members across diverse functional backgrounds to improve operational efficiency
Own and manage total program risk profiles and actionable mitigation plans, regularly synthesizing complex technical and financial trade-offs to present conclusions and strategic recommendations to senior leadership
Synthesize, summarize, and articulate conclusions and recommendations from wide-ranging sources to directly influence program strategy, operational direction, and execution

Required

Bachelor’s degree with 8+ years of experience in program management, project engineering, or technical operations (or Master’s degree with 6+ years of experience, or PhD + 3+ years).
Demonstrated expertise taking primary responsibility for building and maintaining complex integrated master schedules (IMS) and managing large-scale program budgets within technical, aerospace, or advanced hardware environments.
Deep experience across multiple technical domains with a proven ability to independently resolve advanced engineering workflow blockers and critical path constraints.
Recognized communication and leadership skills with a track record of driving cross-functional alignment, building coalitions, and advising senior leadership on strategic program decisions.

This position must meet US export control compliance requirements, therefore a candidate must qualify as a “US Person” as defined by 22 C.F.R.

120.15. “US Person” includes US Citizens, lawful permanent residents, refugees, or asylees.

Desired

Advanced proficiency in developing or selecting modern enterprise program management and schedule tracking systems (e.g., MS Project, Jira, Smartsheet, or Primavera P6)
Broad experience navigating complex aerospace development lifecycles, rapid prototyping environments, or flight test operations
Advanced background in integrated budget forecasting, earned value management (EVM), and variance analysis for large hardware development programs
Experience in the development, procurement, or utilization of military aviation systems

Compensation at Joby is a combination of base pay and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). The target base pay for this position is $182,000 - $250,300/yr. The compensation package will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Joby also offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan with a company match, an employee stock purchase plan (ESPP), short-term and long-term disability coverage, life insurance, and more.

jobs.title: Operations Program Manager 4
jobs.description:
Job Description

The OCI Data Center Build and Deployment organization is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Planning and Deployment Coordinator (PDC) to plan, coordinate, and enable the successful delivery of new data center capacity across multiple locations.

The PDC serves as the critical planning and technical-readiness function between program management, engineering, low-voltage vendors (LVVs), and Data Center Build and Deployment Engineers. The role owns the upfront technical and operational review of deployment projects, ensuring requirements are complete, accurate, executable, and ready for field implementation.

By identifying design gaps, material issues, dependencies, risks, and omissions before work reaches the data hall, the PDC enables field engineers to remain focused on execution, vendor oversight, validation, testing, troubleshooting, and capacity delivery.

The successful candidate will combine deep low-voltage infrastructure knowledge, strong project-management capabilities, technical deployment experience, and effective vendor and stakeholder management.

Required Qualifications & Experience

5+ years experience with data center, telecommunications, or low-voltage infrastructure deployments.
5+ years of structured cabling infrastructure experience, including copper and optical fiber deployment methodologies and industry best practices.
Demonstrated ability to review and validate technical deployment documentation, including cut sheets, patching matrices/schedules, Bills of Materials, rack layouts, and hardware requirements.
Knowledge of network infrastructure, connectivity, networking layers, and testing and validation methodologies.
Experience coordinating or managing low-voltage vendors and contractors in complex deployment environments.
Strong project-management skills, including project scoping, scheduling, dependency management, resource planning, risk management, and critical-path management.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize effectively as requirements and business needs change.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify risks and gaps before affecting delivery schedule.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate technical issues, project status, risks, and required actions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to operate independently while effectively coordinating across multiple teams and stakeholders.

Core Competencies

Planning & Execution: Effectively manages multiple moderately complex deployment activities, establishes clear priorities, monitors milestones and dependencies, and adjusts execution plans as resources, requirements, or schedules change.

Technical Excellence: Applies strong data center and low-voltage infrastructure knowledge to validate deployment requirements, identify technical gaps, and ensure projects are ready for successful field execution.

Ownership & Problem Solving: Proactively identify risk mitigation and project blockers, performs structured analysis, drives issues toward resolution, and escalates appropriately with recommended solutions rather than simply identifying problems.

Collaboration & Stakeholder Management: Builds effective partnerships across technical teams, program management, vendors, and business stakeholders. Establishes clear expectations, communicates proactively, and develops trust through consistent execution and follow-through.

Vendor Management: Establishes clear expectations with vendor partners, monitors execution and quality, identifies gaps, and drives accountability for commitments and corrective actions.

Continuous Improvement: Identifies opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate deployment processes. Develops repeatable mechanisms that improve quality, efficiency, predictability, and delivery velocity.

Continuous Learning: Maintains current knowledge of data center technologies, deployment methodologies, tools, and industry best practices. Seeks feedback and applies lessons learned to improve future execution.

Knowledge Sharing & Development: Shares technical and operational knowledge across the organization, coaches less-experienced team members, contributes to best practices, and participates in candidate interviews and talent development activities.

Success in the Role

Success in this role is demonstrated by the ability to consistently deliver deployment-ready projects to field engineering teams with accurate requirements, validated technical documentation, clear execution plans, identified dependencies, and mitigation risks.

The PDC should reduce the amount of planning and administrative work performed by Data Center Build and Deployment Engineers, allowing field engineers to focus on data-hall execution and technical vendor oversight. Ultimately, the role contributes to faster capacity

delivery, fewer field-discovered issues, improved vendor execution, reduced rework, and more predictable data center deployments.

Responsibilities

Project Planning & Technical Readiness

Ingest new data center build and capacity deployment projects and drive them through deployment readiness.
Conduct comprehensive technical reviews of project requirements before field execution.
Validate hardware requirements, Bills of Materials (BOMs), cut sheets/patching documentation, rack positioning, passive infrastructure, and associated deployment requirements.
Identify technical gaps, omissions, inconsistencies, and dependencies early enough to prevent downstream deployment delays.
Review project scope, schedules, milestones, resources, and critical-path activities to confirm execution readiness.
Coordinate RFQ activities and vendor engagement required to support deployment.
Develop and coordinate early-access plans to maximize deployment readiness and accelerate capacity delivery.
Ensure required materials, documentation, resources, and dependencies are validated before handoff to field engineering teams.

Deployment Execution

Serve as a central coordination point throughout the deployment lifecycle, from project intake through field handoff and capacity delivery.
Partner closely with Data Center Build and Deployment Engineers, Technical Program Managers, Delivery teams, Automation teams, and all relevant other stakeholders to maintain alignment on scope, schedule, dependencies, and execution.
Attend relevant project meetings and translate project-level decisions, changes, risks, and requirements into clear guidance for field engineering stakeholders.
Track milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, and blockers across multiple concurrent projects and data center build deployments.
Proactively identify schedule or execution risks and drive mitigation plans before impacting committed delivery dates.
Escalate critical issues with a clear assessment of impact, identify resolution owners and recommended resolution.
Maintain clear and timely communication regarding project status, risks, decisions, and changes.

Design Change Request Management and Validation

Review Design Change Requests (DCRs) for technical and operational impact.
Coordinate implementation of approved changes across engineering, vendors, program management, and field deployment teams.
Evaluate time bound impacts of changes on materials, cut sheets, BOMs, schedules, resources, and capacity commitments.
Re-establish execution plans and clearly articulate risks and impacts to schedule.
Ensure revised requirements and documentation are accurately communicated to the teams responsible for implementation.

Vendor Management

Coordinate closely with low-voltage vendors to ensure scope, schedules, technical requirements, and quality expectations are clearly understood.
Support RFQ, planning, readiness, and execution activities with vendor partners.
Conduct vendor project and business reviews to evaluate progress, risks, roadblocks, quality, and schedule performance.
Hold vendors accountable for contracted commitments and drive resolution of execution issues.
Partner with field engineers to address technical and operational vendor challenges.
Identify recurring or systemic vendor issues and develop mechanisms to improve quality, predictability, and execution.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate across Engineering, Delivery, Automation, Supply Chain, Program Management, Operations, and vendor organizations to enable seamless capacity delivery.
Provide Technical Program Managers with clear visibility into deployment readiness, progress, dependencies, and risks.
Translate program and design requirements into actionable execution guidance for field teams and vendors.
Build trusted relationships across stakeholder groups and ensure concerns and requirements are identified early.
Facilitate alignment when competing priorities, dependencies, or technical constraints affect delivery.

Process & Continuous Improvement

Develop scalable, repeatable processes and mechanisms that improve deployment quality, speed, and predictability.
Identify recurring deployment defects and address root causes rather than relying on repeated tactical workarounds.
Recommend and implement improvements to planning, technical validation, vendor management, project handoff, and deployment workflows.
Partner with Automation and Program Management teams to identify opportunities to reduce manual effort and improve data and documentation quality.
Document best practices, lessons learned, and standardized deployment processes.
Evaluate the effectiveness of process improvements and their impact on engineering teams, vendors, stakeholders, and delivery performance.

Who We Are

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description

Job Family Definition:

Provides support and/or lead teams through the Engineering development process and implementation of company’s products. Projects are typically shorter-term, less complex and more contained with a defined time frame. Programs are typically longer-term, multi-functional, multi-project with complex requirements and effort. Manage activities, resource capability, schedules, budgets, and ensure cross company communications to facilitate product completion on schedule within budget. Work with engineering management to identify and improve process and program efficiencies. Work can involve external parties such as standards bodies, partners, etc.

Management Level Definition

Contributions impact technical components of HPE products, solutions, or services regularly and sustainable. Applies advanced subject matter knowledge to solve complex business issues and is regarded as a subject matter expert. Provides expertise and partnership to functional and technical project teams and may participate in cross-functional initiatives. Exercises significant independent judgment to determine best method for achieving objectives. May provide team leadership and mentoring to others.

Responsibilities

Manages and leads a program involving multiple functions and project teams to drive the engineering development and implementation process for a product or service offering.
Develops and directs development of schedules, critical deliverables, budget, resource allocation plan, and other support requirements for assigned program.
Manages activities of supporting project teams and internal development partners; ensures progress against established plan and makes determinations based on analysis of business information to alter or update schedule and resource allocation to meet product requirements and development schedule.
Communicates program progress, escalations, and issue analysis to product stakeholders; collaborates with management and internal manufacturing and development partners to recommend and implement changes to product, processes, or business practices to resolve escalated issues, produce solutions, and ensure adherence to budgets and established product roadmaps and schedules
Drives innovation and integration of new technologies and quality initiatives into projects and activities in the manufacturing and/or engineering organization.
Drive Agile execution across multiple cross-functional engineering teams, ensuring alignment on dependencies and release timelines and adapting swiftly to feedback.
Leads and provides guidance and mentoring to less-experienced staff members.

Education And Experience Required

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Management, Engineering, Computer Sciences, or related field
Typically requires 6 - 10 years of relevant experience
Proficiency in Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and implementation processes required
PMP/PMI certification is preferred
3+ years of experience managing complex technical programs using Agile/Scrum methodologies.
Experience with High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments is a plus

Knowledge And Skills

Extensive experience with using project and program planning tools and software packages to create, manage, and track project results.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrated business acumen and successful experience managing all aspects of programs, including communicating with stakeholders and directing matrixed teams and resources.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; mastery in English and local language
Ability to effectively communicate program plans, proposals, and results, and negotiate options at senior management levels.
Ability to understand and translate technical aptitude into practical application
Ability to apply AI for data analysis, research, and content generation
Establish and monitor Agile delivery metrics (such as velocity, burn-down charts, and cumulative flow) to predict delivery timelines and identify systemic bottlenecks.

jobs.title: Cybersecurity Project Manager
jobs.description:
Are you a tech enthusiast who loves solving complex problems?
Do you have a keen eye for detail and excellent analytical skills?
Would your friends describe you as a self-starter who takes pride in your work and enjoys collaborating with others?

If so, we have an exciting opportunity for you at The Greentree Group!

Who We Are

The Greentree Group is a dynamic, innovative, and thriving company that specializes in delivering advanced technology solutions to federal, state, and commercial clients. With a team of highly skilled professionals, we provide cutting-edge services and are always pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

What sets us apart is our commitment to excellence and our passion for the work we do. At The Greentree Group, we are driven by a shared sense of purpose and a desire to make a difference in the lives of people around us. Whether it's helping our clients achieve their goals, developing innovative solutions to complex problems, or giving back to the community, we are dedicated to making a positive impact.

We also believe in investing in our people and providing them with opportunities for growth, development, and advancement. We offer a dynamic and supportive work environment, a culture of continuous learning, and a wide range of benefits and perks that promote work-life balance and personal well-being.

Whether you're a seasoned expert or just starting out in your career, if you're passionate about technology, committed to excellence, and eager to take on new challenges, we want to hear from you!

About The Opportunity

The Greentree Group values its employees and fosters a collaborative environment where talented professionals can thrive. We are seeking an experienced Cybersecurity Project Manager
to lead a complex cybersecurity assessment program supporting a public sector client in Austin, TX.

This role will be responsible for planning, managing, and overseeing cybersecurity assessment activities conducted in accordance with CMS security and privacy requirements, including the Acceptable Risk Controls for ACA, Medicaid, and Partner Entities (ARC-AMPE) framework and applicable NIST standards. The successful candidate will lead assessment teams, manage project schedules and deliverables, coordinate stakeholder communications, and ensure the successful execution of security assessment and authorization activities.

The ideal candidate is a proactive leader who can effectively manage technical teams, communicate with executive stakeholders, translate complex cybersecurity concepts into actionable recommendations, and drive projects to successful completion while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compliance.

Some Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Cybersecurity risks continue to evolve, creating increasingly complex challenges for government agencies responsible for safeguarding sensitive information and critical services. As a Cybersecurity Project Manager, you will play a key role in helping clients understand, assess, and mitigate these risks through structured assessment, compliance, and risk management activities.

Key Responsibilities Include

Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of cybersecurity assessment projects, ensuring adherence to contractual requirements, schedules, budgets, and quality standards.
Manage multidisciplinary assessment teams responsible for evaluating administrative, technical, and operational security controls.
Coordinate security assessment activities conducted under CMS ARC-AMPE, NIST SP 800-53, and other applicable federal and state cybersecurity requirements.
Develop and maintain project management artifacts, including project schedules, risk registers, status reports, action item logs, and executive briefings.
Facilitate meetings and communication between client leadership, technical stakeholders, assessors, and other project participants.
Oversee the development and delivery of assessment documentation, including Security Assessment Plans (SAPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and other required deliverables.
Identify project risks, issues, dependencies, and resource constraints, and develop appropriate mitigation strategies.
Present technical findings, compliance gaps, and risk-based recommendations to both technical and executive audiences.
Support continuous improvement efforts by identifying opportunities to enhance assessment methodologies, project execution processes, and client outcomes.
Ensure project teams maintain compliance with established cybersecurity, privacy, and quality assurance requirements.
The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to the client, helping leadership understand cybersecurity risks, prioritize remediation efforts, and make informed decisions regarding the protection of critical systems and sensitive data.

Minimum Qualifications

Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills.
Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with customers, executive leadership, technical teams, and third-party stakeholders.
Knowledge of cybersecurity industry standards, frameworks, and best practices.
5+ years of experience supporting Security Control Assessments (SCAs), security authorizations, or related cybersecurity compliance activities.
Experience conducting or overseeing technical security audits and assessments for large, complex systems.
Experience presenting security control requirements, assessment results, risks, and deficiencies to both technical and non-technical audiences.
5+ years of project management experience leading cybersecurity, compliance, or assessment engagements.
Experience developing and managing project schedules, budgets, staffing plans, and client deliverables.
Experience identifying, tracking, and mitigating project and cybersecurity risks.
Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-series publications, including assessment of NIST SP 800-53 security controls.
Ability to effectively communicate IT and cybersecurity risks to executive leadership and client stakeholders.
Ability to work independently and lead multidisciplinary teams in a dynamic client environment.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
U.S. Citizenship required.

Desired Qualifications

Experience leading CMS, HHS, or other federal cybersecurity assessment and authorization projects.
Experience supporting Authority to Connect (ATC), Authority to Operate (ATO), continuous monitoring, or related security authorization activities.
Familiarity with CMS ARC-AMPE requirements and controls, as well as legacy MARS-E 2.2 frameworks.
Experience managing distributed assessment teams, subcontractors, and quality review activities.
PMP certification.
CISSP, CISM, CISA, or equivalent cybersecurity certification.
Previous experience supporting government healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, or health insurance exchange systems.

We believe in fostering a positive, inclusive culture that values diversity, teamwork, and personal growth. With opportunities for advancement and a supportive community of colleagues, The Greentree Group is the perfect place to build your career. Learn more about us at www.greentreegroup.com. Please note that this role may require a National Agency Check (NAC) and/or background check, and relocation assistance is not available at this time.

Greentree is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, or status as a qualified individual with a disability or protected veteran.

Compensation / Salary Range:
Greentree adheres to federal, state, and local regulations. This is a Full-Time, Salary, Exempt position. The following salary range is what we reasonably expect to pay but is contingent and subject to a variety of factors, including but not limited to years of experience, education, certification(s), training, specialized skills, responsibilities, etc.

Salary Range:
$125,000 – $145,000

Bonuses:
Greentree has an employee referral bonus, as well as employee bonuses based on employee contributions and Greentree’s yearly performance.

Location:
The Greentree Group’s hiring practices are subject to state-specific business, tax, and employment law considerations. At this time, we are only able to hire candidates who are residents of, and authorized to work in, the following states: AZ, CO, DC, FL, GA, KY, MD, MI, NC, OH, OR, PA, SD, TX, or VA.

Top Benefits

Core Benefits 100% paid by Greentree:
Employee Medical Premium on the High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP), Basic Life Insurance and AD&D, Short-Term Disability (STD), Long-Term Disability (LTD), Health Reimbursement Account (HRA), 401(k) Match, Job-Related Certifications, and Training Programs

Elected Benefits:
Medical, Dental, Vision, HSA, FSA, Voluntary Term Life, 401(k) (Roth and Pretax available)

Time Off: PTO, Flexible Schedules, Holidays and Paid Parental Leave:
Work-life balance is important – we all enjoy some time off for rest and relaxation! Employees receive a very generous amount of PTO which is granted on start date, plus the ability for quick escalation to the next tier. Flexible/hybrid working schedules and 11 paid holidays, in addition to paid parental leave round out the work-life balance benefits.

Paid Training and Development:
We encourage and support ongoing employee learning and development, consistent with needs of the company, its clients, and markets. Greentree is committed to paying the cost for job-related certifications and/or training programs. In conjunction with management/employee communication and discussions regarding performance and goals, employees are expected to seek out and pursue development opportunities to meet emerging organizational skill requirements in combination with their own personal growth needs. Greentree also makes job-related tuition reimbursement contributions for those in higher-level education programs.

Meetings and Events Senior Project Manager

Brand:
Emota

Location:
Philadelphia or hybrid on Central or Eastern time

Reporting to:
Project Director

Direct reports:
Project Co-ordinators and Senior Project Co-ordinators

A Bit About The Role …

As an experienced Senior Project Manager specializing in Meetings and Events, you will play an important role in the planning of global projects for our renowned clients.

You will use your project management skills to achieve all logistical elements and associated budgets of our projects, whilst mentoring our Project Co-ordinators to follow the same.

Your role, which includes national and international travel, will involve client, partner, supplier, team, and financial management at all stages of the delivery - pre, on-site and post event.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package to you including volunteer days, enhanced annual leave with an option to buy/sell, 401k, health insurance and many other benefits.

You will…

Project Management

Lead the project from a client, internal team and external partner perspective
Lead small to medium sized projects that involve several Emota / XD service lines, being the main contact for the client and ensuring a seamless delivery
Ensure that the highest standards of event planning and delivery are maintained through the leadership of Project Executives
Oversee the building of apps and content
Manage post event metric reporting
Manage all hotels and venues and associated logistical arrangements.
Co-ordinate client requirements with all 3rd party suppliers, promoting relationships
Manage communications e.g. weekly status reports to all internal and external partners
Travel on-site to conduct site inspections including planning meetings with all suppliers and for delivery of the event
Attend on-site at Meetings and Events held both nationally and internationally

Summary Of Position

The Staff Technical Program Manager (TPM)
resides within the Product and Technology organization and drives the end-to-end delivery of complex, cross-functional technical programs and strategic initiatives. This role requires deep technical expertise, strategic thinking, and the ability to influence outcomes across a highly matrixed organization. Working closely with Product Management, Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, and Operations teams, this leader drives alignment, mitigates risk, and delivers measurable business outcomes.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Lead complex technical programs spanning web, mobile, medical device, embedded software, firmware, and data platforms.
Drive end-to-end program execution from initiation through launch, ensuring stakeholder alignment across all milestones.

Manage technical dependencies, risks, issues, and mitigation plans across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Facilitate technical discussions regarding architecture decisions, systems integration, platform scalability, and design tradeoffs.
Partner with senior engineers and architects to align program execution with technical roadmap objectives and platform evolution.
Develop and maintain program dashboards, status reports, key performance indicators, and executive communications.
Apply Lean, Agile, Scrum, Kanban, and continuous improvement methodologies to deliver predictable outcomes.
Leverage AI-powered tools and automation to improve program reporting, risk identification, dashboard creation, and operational efficiency.
Establish and track program success metrics, ensuring measurable outcomes and transparent progress reporting.
Drive stakeholder communication, influence decision-making, and resolve blockers through collaboration and negotiation.

Candidates with additional questions or concerns regarding any recruiting communications or Kapitus’ recruiting process in general should email recruiting@kapitus.com

Kapitus is building a next-generation enterprise data and AI capability that replaces hundreds of legacy analytics workflows with governed, reusable business data products and moves the organization from producing reports to producing decisions.

We are looking for an experienced Technical Program Manager to run the day-to-day execution of this program. This is not a status-reporting role. You will own the integrated delivery plan across concurrent workstreams data architecture and platform engineering, governed business data products, MDM and ontology, semantic and consumption layers, data governance, ML/MLOps, and GenAI/agentic AI. This will be delivered by a mix of internal teams and external consulting partners across onshore, nearshore, and offshore locations. You will keep a milestone-gated, tightly budgeted program on schedule, hold vendors to their commitments, and be credible in front of both engineers and executives.

You report directly to the program executive leading the Data & AI organization and serve as the operational execution lead for the transformation program. You are not the architect, the product owner, the engineering lead, or the Scrum Master; you are the person who turns architecture decisions into plans, plans into accountable work, and work into accepted, evidenced outcomes.

What You Will Do

Program delivery and planning

Own and maintain the single authoritative integrated delivery plan across internal teams and all delivery partners — reconciling vendor plans into one program baseline rather than managing independent project schedules — covering sequencing, cross-stream dependencies, critical path, resource loading and capacity, and milestone readiness.
Own end-to-end readiness of each data product delivery wave: design, source readiness, build, governance controls, verification, business validation, serving and consumption readiness, production release, and legacy decommissioning. Code complete is not product complete.
Run the program’s delivery cadence end to end — sprint ceremonies, backlog alignment across streams, RAID (risks, actions, issues, decisions) management, and weekly executive reporting.
Manage milestone-gated delivery: track work against defined acceptance gates (design baseline, ready-to-build, vendor verification, business/customer validation, production acceptance, closeout) and make sure nothing is claimed complete that has not passed its gate.
Track budget consumption against not-to-exceed envelopes and estimate-at-completion forecasts; surface variances early with options, not surprises.
Plan realistically — distinguish contracted capacity from productive capacity, and keep utilization assumptions explicit and defensible.

Vendor and partner management

Manage day-to-day execution with external consulting partners: statement-of-work scope, deliverable acceptance, change control, and separation of duties between build and validation teams.
Coordinate distributed teams across time zones and keep handoffs between onshore design and offshore engineering clean.
Prepare the evidence trail — delivery plans, defect logs, verification records — that supports invoice approval and milestone release decisions.
Maintain traceability from contractual deliverables through program requirements, epics and stories, acceptance criteria, validation evidence, milestone gates, and commercial approvals — so every invoice correlates to accepted work.

Technical coordination

Understand the work well enough to challenge it: data product design, ELT pipeline builds, legacy workflow migration and decommissioning, semantic layer and BI serving, data quality and governance controls, and ML/AI platform components.
Run dependency management between platform hardening, data product waves, governance readiness, and AI platform build-out.
Coordinate governance readiness alongside product delivery — ownership, critical-data-element and sensitivity classification, lineage, data quality controls, metadata, policy conformance, and catalog readiness — so governance ships with the product rather than following it months later.
Manage cross-functional readiness dependencies spanning architecture, security/risk, platform, governance, procurement, and production operations; ensure approvals and unresolved decisions are visible on the critical path and driven to closure.
Facilitate architecture and design decision forums; track exceptions and conformance debt to closure.

Stakeholder management

Be the connective tissue between business owners, architecture, engineering, governance, finance/procurement, and executive sponsors.
Communicate program status in plain language — accurate, evidence-based, and honest about risk.
Drive closure, not coordination alone: drive timely decisions, identify accountable owners, escalate unresolved dependencies early, and challenge unsupported status or completion claims.

What We’re Looking For

10+ years delivering complex technology programs
5+ years leading enterprise data/platform transformation programs involving multiple concurrent technical teams. Backgrounds that combine program leadership with engineering management, technical delivery, consulting, data platform delivery, or solution delivery are strongly valued; demonstrated technical delivery depth matters more than title progression alone.
Consulting or professional services delivery background. You have run client-facing programs under tight timelines, fixed budgets, and contractual milestone commitments, and you know how to manage scope, change control, and acceptance in that environment (either side of the table: delivery firm or client program office).
Deep, practiced agile delivery skills with Scrum, Kanban, and scaled/hybrid models; you can run ceremonies, coach teams, manage backlogs across multiple pods, and blend agile execution with milestone-gated commercial governance.
Modern cloud data platform fluency and hands-on program experience with Snowflake and/or Databricks, and working knowledge of the surrounding ecosystem: ELT/transformation frameworks (e.g., dbt), orchestration, data catalogs and lineage tooling, BI/semantic layers, and legacy workflow migration (e.g., Alteryx, SSIS, or similar).
Strong AI/ML literacy, you understand the ML lifecycle (feature engineering, training, validation, deployment, monitoring), MLOps concepts, and the emerging GenAI/LLM stack (retrieval, agents, model risk considerations) well enough to plan and de-risk AI workstreams.
Vendor management experience managing multi-vendor delivery against SOWs, rate cards, and NTE budgets, including offshore/nearshore delivery models.
Financial discipline comfortable owning budget tracking, forecasting (EAC), and the commercial mechanics of T&M and milestone-based contracts.
Excellent communication skills with crisp written and verbal communication; able to produce executive-ready status materials and defend the numbers behind them.

Additional Preferred Skills

Experience in financial services in lending, banking, fintech, or another regulated environment and familiarity with model risk management and data governance expectations in regulated industries.
Experience with data product operating models (data mesh / data product thinking, data contracts, certified metrics).
Certifications such as PMP, PMI-ACP, CSM/A-CSM, SAFe, or equivalent are valued as evidence of rigor, not as a substitute for demonstrated delivery experience.
Snowflake, Databricks, or cloud (AWS/Azure) certifications.
Experience standing up program governance from scratch: gate definitions, RAID discipline, delivery evidence standards, and vendor validation streams.

You’ll establish the plans and operating structures needed to move work forward, align technical and operational teams, drive decisions, manage dependencies and risks, and ensure stakeholders are prepared for launches.

Because we build new products from the ground up, the work does not end when a product launches. You’ll own ongoing engagement with users, including onboarding, training, hands-on support, and creating clear ways for people to share feedback. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how our products fit into users’ day-to-day work, what is working, and where they are struggling. You’ll bring those insights back to product, design, and engineering so the team can iterate quickly toward product-market fit.

You’ll also help keep the team aligned with its broader objectives. You’ll maintain a clear view of priorities, progress, dependencies, risks, and outcomes across the portfolio and provide clear updates and recommendations to team and company leadership.

In This Role, You Will

Independently lead complex, high-priority technical programs from early planning through launch, adoption, and ongoing iteration.
Partner with product and engineering leadership to translate strategy and team objectives into clear, executable plans.
Establish program structures, decision-making forums, operating cadences, and accountability across multiple teams.
Align product, design, engineering, data, operations, and other stakeholders around priorities, responsibilities, and delivery plans.

Identify gaps in strategy or execution, develop recommendations, and drive the decisions needed to move work forward.
Anticipate risks and blockers, clarify tradeoffs, resolve disagreements, and escalate decisions when needed.
Own communication, enablement, change management, and rollout strategies for new products and workflows.
Lead post-launch user engagement through onboarding, training, office hours, hands-on support, and other programs that drive adoption.
Build trusted relationships with users and create an environment where they provide frequent, candid feedback.
Observe how products fit into real workflows and identify points of confusion, friction, or unmet need.
Combine user feedback, usage data, and operational signals to understand what is working and what needs to change.
Translate user insights into clear themes and actionable recommendations for product, design, and engineering.
Create tight feedback loops that help the team test assumptions, learn quickly, and iterate toward product-market fit.
Define and track program health, adoption, user sentiment, and operational outcomes.
Maintain visibility into priorities, progress, dependencies, and risks across the team’s portfolio.
Prepare clear, decision-oriented updates and recommendations for senior leadership.
Improve the team’s planning and execution practices while keeping processes lightweight.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have 7+ years of experience in technical program management, product operations, or a similar role leading complex software initiatives.
Have independently led multiple high-impact programs involving several technical and business teams.
Have helped take new software products from early planning through launch, adoption, and rapid iteration toward product-market fit.
Are energized by working directly with users and willing to provide hands-on support while a product is still new.
Know how to build trust with users, ask good questions, and get candid feedback about what is and is not working.
Can identify patterns across qualitative feedback, usage data, and operational signals and turn them into actionable recommendations.
Have strong technical fluency and can partner with engineers on architecture, integrations, data dependencies, security, reliability, and delivery tradeoffs.
Have led significant operational or organizational change alongside technical product delivery.
Can influence senior leaders, drive difficult decisions, and build alignment across teams with competing priorities.
Identify and address strategic or execution gaps without waiting for detailed direction.
Communicate clearly and directly across technical teams, operational partners, users, and executives.
Can move comfortably between organizational strategy and detailed, hands-on execution
Bring structure to fast-moving work without adding unnecessary process.
Are curious about how AI can change the way organizations operate and how people work.

Location: Torrance, CA

Position Summary

We are seeking a Senior IT Project Manager – Data Privacy & Compliance to lead large-scale regulatory, privacy, and compliance initiatives within a complex enterprise environment. This role will be responsible for driving cross-functional programs focused on privacy compliance, regulatory readiness, governance, risk management, and enterprise policy implementation while partnering closely with Legal, Compliance, Security, IT, and business stakeholders.

The ideal candidate combines strong project and program management expertise with experience leading privacy-related initiatives, managing enterprise budgets, and delivering complex regulatory programs within highly regulated environments.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead end-to-end delivery of enterprise privacy and compliance initiatives including CCPA, CPRA, AADC, ADA, and related regulatory programs
• Develop and manage project plans, schedules, budgets, forecasts, milestones, and governance activities
• Manage multiple cross-functional workstreams and project teams to ensure successful project delivery
• Drive implementation of privacy controls, governance frameworks, and compliance processes across the organization
• Ensure alignment with privacy regulations, internal policies, audit requirements, and industry standards
• Monitor project performance, identify risks, and proactively manage issues, dependencies, and mitigation plans
• Track project budgets, perform variance analysis, and provide financial forecasts and recommendations to leadership
• Create executive-level presentations, dashboards, status reports, and steering committee updates
• Build strong relationships with executive leadership, Legal, Compliance, Information Security, IT, and business stakeholders
• Support requirements gathering, backlog prioritization, and project planning activities
• Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable project plans and implementation roadmaps
• Support audit readiness efforts and regulatory assessments by maintaining project documentation and compliance evidence
• Manage release planning, deployment activities, production support coordination, and post-launch stabilization efforts
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives and establish privacy program and project management best practices

What You'll Be Working On

• Enterprise privacy compliance initiatives
• CCPA, CPRA, AADC, ADA, and regulatory readiness programs
• Data privacy governance and policy implementation
• Privacy-by-design initiatives
• Cross-functional IT, Legal, Compliance, and Security projects
• Project portfolio governance and executive reporting

Required Skills & Experience

• Proven experience leading large-scale, cross-functional enterprise initiatives
• Strong understanding of privacy regulations and compliance program delivery
• Experience managing project budgets, forecasts, timelines, resources, and governance activities
• Experience gathering requirements and managing complex stakeholder environments
• Strong understanding of Agile, Waterfall, and Hybrid SDLC methodologies
• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills
• Strong executive communication, presentation, and stakeholder management capabilities
• Experience managing multiple priorities in fast-paced enterprise environments
• Stable work history within large enterprise organizations
• Experience with privacy platforms such as OneTrust or similar technologies

• Experience translating regulatory requirements into business and technical implementation plans
• Experience supporting audit readiness, regulatory reviews, and compliance assessments
• Strong program governance and financial management experience
• 3+ years of Big 4 consulting experience preferred
• Experience working within highly regulated enterprise environments

BAE Systems is an organization anchored by its purpose. We’re dedicated to defending national security while pushing the limits of technology. Here, your connection to our shared mission will propel you, and our future forward. Our supply chain team is at the heart of our operational success, ensuring that the critical components and services required to protect our service members are delivered with precision and excellence.

We are looking for a

Supply Chain Program Manager

to join our team and serve as a strategic leader for select programs. In a company like ours, everything we do matters—and that certainly applies to our Supply Chain Program Managers. You will act as the primary conduit for supply chain strategy and execution, collaborating across functional teams to drive resolution and deliver meaningful results.
