new_jobs.description:
About XCures

The best of medicine should belong to everyone. Nobody dreams of becoming good at being a patient. We have people to love, things we want to do, and plans we hope to keep. Illness already asks enough of us.

xCures® exists to give healthcare the capacity to care for everyone. Healthcare has more to give. Too much of its time, money, and talent goes into unnecessary work that keeps people waiting and drives up the cost of care. Freeing those resources can make excellent care possible for far more people.

xCures understands a patient’s history across the places they receive care and keeps that understanding current. It puts trusted information in the hands of the people who need it, when they need it, and uses that knowledge to take on more of the administrative work around care. Every extracted data point traces back to the exact document and page it came from.

Our ambition is to empower doctors to make better decisions, enable researchers to develop better treatments faster, and help healthcare organizations serve more people with fewer errors and lower costs. We work with diagnostic labs, providers, telehealth companies, health systems, payers, and consumer health platforms. We are a fully remote, venture-backed team that holds itself to the same standard as our product: trustworthy, precise, and purposeful.

We are building for the lives people want to live.

Here’s Where You’ll Make An Impact

xCures is hiring a Technical Program Manager to run the operating system of its Customer Solutions team, the group that sits between our customers, our platform, and the engineers who connect them. You will report to the Director, Customer Solutions, with a dotted line to the Program Management Office. Your job is to make delivery visible, predictable, and measurable: what is coming in, what is committed, where it stands, and when a customer goes live.

The team ships AI-native tooling and customer integrations quickly, and it needs someone who can turn that pace into a clear picture for Revenue Leadership and the PMO while keeping the engineers building instead of coordinating. You will sit between customers, Engineering, Product, and Customer Success on work that puts the patient history in front of the clinician who needs it. If you want to own the systems a team runs on rather than inherit them, this is that job.

Key Responsibilities

Own delivery reporting for Customer Solutions: maintain the single source of truth on program status, risks, and dates, and deliver a regular cadence of updates to Revenue Leadership, the PMO, and executives
Manage intake and triage of inbound requests from Sales, Customer Success, and Product, coordinating prioritization and routing decisions and communicating outcomes back to the people who asked
Track active customer integration and onboarding programs from kickoff to go-live, surfacing blockers early and holding the team to committed dates
Build and maintain internal and external technical training, product guides, and support resources so customers and colleagues can self-serve
Define success metrics, dashboards, and feedback loops for the team's tools and integrations, and use them to show adoption and performance
Work with Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and the PMO to keep Customer Solutions work aligned with platform priorities and company delivery standards
First 90 days: stand up the intake and triage process and take over program tracking for every active customer integration
First year: predictable, measurable delivery across all Customer Solutions programs and a faster contract-to-live cycle, measured by on-time delivery against committed dates, time from contract to live integration, and customer and internal stakeholder satisfaction

Qualifications

Required:

3+ years in technical program management, product operations, or project management in a technology environment
Track record of leading cross-functional initiatives from definition through delivery
Experience working with both engineering teams and customer-facing roles, and translating between them
Technical acumen and curiosity: able to engage substantively on APIs, data pipelines, cloud infrastructure, and AI and LLM tooling
Experience creating training materials and technical documentation for technical and non-technical audiences
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

Bonus Points

Healthcare, diagnostics, or health IT background
Hands-on use of agentic AI tools in your daily work
Enterprise SaaS onboarding or implementation experience
Scripting or light automation skills

Location

xCures operates in a distributed, remote-first environment, with occasional travel to company offsites or key meetings throughout the year. Candidates may be located anywhere in the United States. The successful candidate must already have authorization to work in the United States. At this time, xCures does not offer sponsorship. All candidate information will be held in confidence and in accordance with EEOC guidelines.

Additional Considerations

We recognize that people bring a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the requirements listed in a job description. Diversity of experience and skills, combined with a shared passion for healthcare, is what drives us to innovate. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification listed. xCures is an equal opportunity employer, committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Benefits

Great work deserves great support. We believe our people are our greatest asset, and we’re committed to supporting them with a strong, competitive benefits package. Our goal is to be a place where people genuinely want to build their careers, and our benefits are designed to support our team in the ways that matter most.

And more!

new_jobs.description:
Description

Join Team CARFAX as Onboarding Program Manager

Why Mobility Global?

At Mobility Global, our mission is to provide the trusted information that helps billions of people build, sell, and own vehicles with confidence. As we shape the next generation of automotive intelligence through innovation, AI, and industry-leading data, we are creating new opportunities for our customers, our business, and our people.

CARFAX, a division of Mobility Global, helps millions of people every day confidently shop, buy, service and sell used cars with innovative solutions powered by CARFAX vehicle history information. CARFAX is nationally recognized as a top workplace by The Washington Post and Glassdoor.com. Shop, Buy, Service, Sell – Show me the CARFAX™.

10X Virginia Business Best Places to Work
9X Washingtonian Great Places to Work
10X Washington Post Top Workplace
3X St. Louis Post-Dispatch Best Places to Work

About The Role

At CARFAX, how quickly and consistently new hires reach productivity is a direct revenue imperative — and the Onboarding Program Manager owns that outcome. You’ll design, build, and run structured onboarding for every revenue-generating and customer-facing team in the DBU: Sales (Field, Strategic, and Inside), Customer Care, and Service/Account Management.

A central goal is consistency. Today, onboarding varies depending on which manager a new hire reports to — you’ll create a standard, repeatable approach within each team (so every Field Sales director ramps new reps the same way) while keeping each team’s distinct needs intact. You’ll facilitate monthly in-person sessions at CARFAX’s Reston, VA headquarters, build the content new hires rely on, and partner closely with internal teams to ensure new hires receive the most relevant content.

At CARFAX, we believe in the power of teamwork and value in-person interactions so that we can collaborate and thrive together. This position will require 3-4 days a week in our Virginia office subject to change with future business needs.

What You’ll Be Doing

Own onboarding end-to-end for all DBU teams. Own the new hire experience for Sales (Field, Strategic, and Inside), Customer Care, and Service/Account Management, building programs that reflect each team’s distinct roles, tools, and success metrics. Assess the existing program, keep what works, and build on the rest.
Standardize onboarding within each team. Create a consistent, repeatable approach for each team so every new hire gets the same experience regardless of their manager — while preserving the meaningful differences between teams.
Design and own role-specific pathways and milestones. Build structured learning journeys for each role, from pre-boarding through full ramp. You own how long onboarding runs and what “ready” means, anchoring each pathway to clear milestones so you can track progress and intervene early when someone falls behind.
Facilitate monthly onboarding sessions and role-plays at HQ. Lead structured, high-energy in-person sessions at Reston HQ each month — role-plays, skills practice, objection handling, and live dealer simulations. The best programs are practice-heavy, not information-dumps, so reps build skill through repetition and feedback before their first live call.
Create and maintain high-quality onboarding content. Own all onboarding materials — learning paths, playbooks, decks, quick-reference guides, role-play scripts, and certifications — polished, current, and built for how people actually learn. Requires strong PowerPoint and content-creation skills.
Partner closely with the Sales Enablement Lead. Make the handoff from onboarding to ongoing enablement seamless — one continuous journey, not a cliff. Your programs should set up their work, not duplicate it.
Measure what matters and continuously improve. Track time-to-productivity, ramp time by role, cohort trends, manager satisfaction, and new-hire feedback, and use them to decide what to keep, cut, or rebuild. Completion rates are a baseline, not a success metric.
Collaborate cross-functionally and leverage experts. Partner with HR on pre-boarding, Marketing and Product on product knowledge, and RevOps on milestones and KPIs. Maintain a network of internal SMEs who keep programs accurate, making their involvement easy rather than a burden.

Required

What we’re looking for:

5+ years of experience designing, building, and leading structured onboarding programs — ideally across multiple teams or roles within a single organization.
Demonstrated success reducing time-to-productivity and improving new hire ramp outcomes, with data to support it.
A track record of standardizing programs across managers or locations to reduce variance in the new-hire experience.
Experience taking an existing program and improving it — assessing what’s working, keeping what is, and rebuilding what isn’t — rather than only building from a blank page.
Strong live facilitation skills — you are at your best in front of a room, leading a role-play, running a skills certification, or coaching a new hire in real time.
Exceptional content-creation skills, including the ability to build polished, well-designed learning materials, onboarding decks, and training presentations in PowerPoint (or equivalent tools) that are clear, compelling, and field-ready.
Experience building role-specific, milestone-based onboarding pathways tailored to distinct job functions.
Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously — this role serves multiple teams with different cycles, content needs, and go-live moments.
Ability to travel up to 15% of the time to support field team onboarding, regional events, and key team milestones.
Experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders (HR, Sales Leadership, RevOps, Marketing) to build programs that are accurate, aligned, and well-supported.

Preferred

Local to the Northern Virginia/DC metro area and able to work from CARFAX’s Reston, VA headquarters on a regular basis — monthly onboarding sessions are in-person, and proximity to HQ makes a meaningful difference in this role.
Automotive industry or automotive technology experience; understanding how dealerships operate and how CARFAX’s products serve them is a genuine advantage.
Experience supporting onboarding across a blend of commercial roles — sales, customer service, and account/service management.
Familiarity with learning management systems (LMS), content management tools, and conversation intelligence platforms (e.g., Gong, Chorus).
Experience with a revenue enablement platform (e.g., Allego, Highspot, Seismic) and a CRM (preferably Salesforce).

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is $100,000 - $140,000. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on a variety of factors, including geographic location, relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

Carfax is committed to providing competitive compensation that reflects local market conditions and individual contributions. In addition to base salary, employees may be eligible for incentive compensation, long-term incentives, and a comprehensive benefits package, where applicable.

About CARFAX And S&P Global Mobility

S&P Global has recently announced the intent to separate our Mobility Segment into a standalone public company.

CARFAX, part of S&P Global Mobility, helps millions of people every day confidently shop, buy, service and sell used cars with innovative solutions powered by CARFAX vehicle history information. The expert in vehicle history since 1984, CARFAX provides exclusive services like CARFAX Used Car Listings, CARFAX Car Care, CARFAX History-Based Value and the flagship CARFAX® Vehicle History Report™ to consumers and the automotive industry. CARFAX owns the world’s largest vehicle history database and is nationally recognized as a top workplace by The Washington Post and Glassdoor.com. Shop, Buy, Service, Sell – Show me the CARFAX™. S&P Global Mobility is a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI). S&P Global is the world’s foremost provider of credit ratings, benchmarks, analytics and workflow solutions in the global capital, commodity and automotive markets.
